## Where is conflict concentrated, and how has it changed?

The study follows **53,805 conflict events across 330 Myanmar townships over 57 months**.

- Local Moran’s I identifies clusters and outliers.
- Gi* identifies hotspots and coldspots.
- Mann–Kendall and EHSA examine their changes through time.
- Separate comparisons examine civilian targeting and reported deaths.

::: {.small-note}
Sources: [ACLED Myanmar](https://acleddata.com/country/myanmar), supplied through eLearn; [MIMU v9.4](https://geonode.themimu.info/layers/geonode:mmr_polbnda_adm3_250k_mimu_1). Counts describe recorded events, not risk per person.
:::

## The monthly total peaks in late 2023

![](take-home-02/figures/monthly.png){height=430 alt="Monthly conflict counts by event type."}

January–September 2025 has **12.4% fewer events** than the same months of 2024. Explosions and remote violence remain the largest category.

## 127 townships recorded increases

![](take-home-02/figures/recent-changes.png){height=480 alt="Map of changes between January to September 2024 and 2025, with the five largest township rises and falls."}

Kawkareik, Kyaukpyu and Nawnghkio had the largest rises. Rakhine’s total fell by **734**, while Kyaukpyu, within Rakhine, added **207**.

## Maungdaw ranks higher for reported deaths

![](take-home-02/figures/events-and-deaths.png){height=450 alt="Reported deaths by township and comparison with event counts."}

Maungdaw ranks **17th by incidents but third by reported deaths** (1,583). Kale has the highest reported death toll (1,877).

::: {.small-note}
Reported estimates across retained conflict events, including combatant deaths. These are not civilian death totals.
:::

## Clusters and outliers

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="67%"}
![](take-home-02/figures/local-association.png){height=570 alt="Local Moran’s I and Gi-star results."}
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
Gi* identifies **38 hotspots**:

- 18 in Sagaing;
- seven in Mandalay;
- six in Magway.

Local Moran’s I finds 38 high–high clusters, 52 low–low clusters and four low–high outliers.

::: {.small-note}
Queen neighbours; 999 permutations; p < 0.05. Grey means no significant result.
:::
:::
:::

## Following concentrations through time

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="67%"}
![](take-home-02/figures/ehsa.png){height=570 alt="Mann–Kendall trends and emerging hotspot patterns."}
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
The full EHSA classification finds **26 oscillating** and **eight sporadic hotspots**.

Of these, 23 also have significant trends and appear here.

An area can have many earlier hot months without being a hotspot at the September 2025 endpoint.

::: {.small-note}
Current and preceding month; whole-cube Gi* reference. Map restricted to trend p < 0.05.
:::
:::
:::

## New hotspots around Kawkareik

![](take-home-02/figures/hotspots-two-periods.png){height=440 alt="Gi-star hotspots in matched January to September periods of 2024 and 2025."}

Five of the seven 2025-only hotspots border Kawkareik. Hlaingbwe rises from **one to 41 events** and retains its hotspot status after the multiple-test adjustment.

::: {.small-note}
Same months and Queen neighbours; 9,999 permutations. A change in classification is not a direct test of change between years.
:::

## The civilian-targeting pattern

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="67%"}
![](take-home-02/figures/civilian-hotspots.png){height=570 alt="Gi-star maps for all retained records and the civilian-targeting subset."}
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**16,391 events** in the retained data targeted civilians.

Their map has **37 hotspots**, with 34 overlapping the overall conflict hotspots.

Hakha, Tonzang and Nawnghkio appear only in the civilian-targeting hotspot map.

In the matched 2024 and 2025 periods, civilian-targeting events fell by only **2%**. In **26 townships**, they rose while total events fell.

::: {.small-note}
These are events targeting civilians, not civilian deaths. The flag excludes incidental civilian harm.
:::
:::
:::

## How much confidence should we place in the maps?

- Adjusting for multiple tests reduces the overall Gi* hotspots from **38 to 19**.
- Gi* classifications agree in **87.2%** of townships under a different neighbour definition.
- Checking related months reduces significant trends from **218 to 148**; **126** remain after also adjusting for multiple tests.
- Kawkareik and Nawnghkio retain evidence of upward trends under the stronger checks.

Reporting gaps, approximate locations and different township sizes remain limitations. A low count or grey area does not establish safety.

## Recommended actions

- In **Sagaing, Mandalay and Magway**, compare hotspot townships with aid coverage and identify communities still waiting for food, shelter or medical support.
- In **Kawkareik, Kyaukpyu and Nawnghkio**, ask local aid groups whether displacement has increased demand beyond what they can provide. Include **Hlaingbwe** and the other neighbours of Kawkareik.
- In **Kale and Maungdaw**, follow up on high reported death tolls with local clinics and aid groups to identify unmet household needs.
- In **Monywa**, check displaced households’ housing, food and healthcare needs before reducing any existing aid.
- In **Pakokku and Myaing**, follow up on rising civilian targeting despite falling total counts. Check incidents around **Hakha, Tonzang and Nawnghkio** as well.

Update the records beyond September 2025 and confirm current needs with local aid groups before acting.

::: {.small-note}
[Full report, sources and code](take-home-exercise-02.qmd) · [Coursework repository](https://github.com/chinh02/isss626-chinh-le)
:::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
